single.reason: The T-rich reference allele is more compatible with a TCF/LEF motif than the G allele, and TCF7L2 is active in colorectal cancer cells and can regulate epithelial genes such as CLDN1.
CDX2 commonly recognizes A/T-rich intestinal regulatory motifs, so replacing T with G is more likely to weaken its binding in this colorectal context.
The G allele could contribute to an ETS-family recognition core if the surrounding sequence supplies the required flanking bases, potentially altering CLDN1 regulation.
